meeting_header: Date: 2025-08-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Redwood: Maya Patel (AE), Carlos Reyes (SE) | Customer: Janelle Morris (CISO), Tariq Khan (Platform Eng), Leah Park (Legal Ops)
summary: Introductory security intake focusing on whether Oakview should use Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. Key concerns: SOC2/ISO proof, SSO/SAML + SCIM lifecycle, RBAC model, audit logs & retention, KMS/heirarchy and customer key ownership, and data residency. Team agreed to share certs and a demo tenant; schedule a technical pilot deep-dive next week.
topics: Encryption and KMS customer key ownership
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood team. With me is Carlos, our systems SE. How are you all?
[00:06] Janelle: Hi, I'm Janelle, CISO at Oakview. Good, thanks. We only have 45 minutes so we'll jump in.
[00:12] Tariq: Tariq here, platform engineering. We've been looking at a few inference vendors, wanted to clarify security posture before any pilots.
[00:19] Leah: Leah from legal, I'll mostly listen for data residency and retention questions.
[00:24] Carlos: Great. Quick agenda: SOC/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC examples, audit logs & retention, KMS and key ownership, then tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[00:35] Janelle: Perfect. Starting with compliance — do you have up-to-date SOC 2 and any ISO 27001? We need to see those artifacts before security sign-off.
[00:44] Maya: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II for our control plane and ISO 27001 attestation — I can share the certs and our control matrix after the call. We'll redact client names where needed.
[00:52] Janelle: Okay, we need the scope — does SOC 2 cover the Hosted service only or Dedicated as well? What's in scope for Private?
[01:01] Carlos: Good question. For Hosted, our SOC2 covers our managed control plane and hosted inference endpoints. Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) are covered under the same control framework but with different isolation controls — we can provide a supplemental description. For Private (VPC/on-prem), the customer-managed components fall under the customer's controls; Redwood provides guidance and connectors but we don't include customer-controlled infra in our SOC scope.
[01:23] Tariq: So for Private on-prem, we need to run our own audit controls. That aligns with what we thought. For Dedicated, do you support bringing-your-own VPC?
[01:33] Maya: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private networking. We'll provide network diagrams.
[01:38] Leah: Any certifications around penetration testing or external vuln scans that we can include in our vendor risk?
[01:44] Carlos: We run annual third-party pen tests and vulnerability scanning; we have summary reports and remediation timelines. I'll attach a redacted exec summary.
[01:52] Janelle: Good. Moving to identity — SSO is a hard requirement. We use an IdP (Okta). Do you support SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
[02:01] Maya: Yes, SAML for auth and SCIM for provisioning. We also support SCIM group sync and automatic deprovisioning. Carlos, do you want to add specifics on session length and cert rotation?
[02:11] Carlos: Sure. Session TTLs are configurable per-tenant; SAML cert rotation can be automated via metadata exchange or manual rotate if customers prefer. For Dedicated/Private we can expose SAML endpoints into your auth plane. Also note, our RBAC primitives map to groups and policies; we'll show role examples in the demo tenant.
[02:28] Tariq: On RBAC — we want least privilege. Can you scope tokens to model family or route-level permissions?
[02:35] Carlos: Yes. Tokens can be scoped to API routes, model access, and even per-route rate limits. You can create roles like inference-read, inference-write, admin, etc. The UI and API both support role bindings. We'll provision sample roles.
[02:47] Janelle: Audit logging — how long do you retain logs by default and can we export them to our SIEM?
[02:54] Maya: Default retention for request-level audit logs is 90 days. We can configure longer retention as an add-on. Logs are streamable to customer S3 buckets or to SIEMs via our log export (supports syslog/forwarders).
[03:07] Tariq: We need immutable audit trails and tamper evidence; does Redwood support write-once logs or signed log chains?
[03:13] Carlos: We don't currently offer write-once storage as a first-class feature in Hosted, but we can integrate with customer-managed S3 with policy locks or ship logs to an append-only store. For Dedicated/Private, customers can implement their own WORM storage. We do provide signed log entries with SHA hashes for critical events in the control plane — I'll follow up with the exact schema.
[03:33] Leah: Retention policy — our legal team requires 7 years for certain data types. Can Redwood accommodate that?
[03:40] Maya: For logs and request metadata, yes but that becomes an add-on and affects cost. For raw request/response payloads, we have opt-in data retention for troubleshooting; otherwise, payload retention is disabled by default for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private you can choose to persist payloads as you see fit.
[03:58] Janelle: Encryption — what's your default? Are data at rest and in transit encrypted? Who manages the KMS keys?
[04:05] Carlos: TLS in transit across all products. At rest we use envelope encryption. Default is Redwood-managed keys in a cloud KMS. We support customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or GCP KMS for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private/on-prem, customers fully manage keys. If you require HSM-backed keys with customer key ownership, that's possible in Dedicated via BYOK workflows.
[04:25] Tariq: Important: we require customer-controlled key rotation and key destruction logs. Can we do that in Hosted?
[04:31] Carlos: With CMK integration, you control the master key and rotation policies; Redwood never has access to the plaintext master key. We'll capture KMS audit logs and can stream them to your account.
[04:41] Janelle: What about model KV cache and memory — any chance of leakage across tenants?
[04:47] Carlos: Isolation is a big focus. For Hosted, we use tenant isolation at the runtime level, and KV cache is partitioned. There's no cross-tenant sharing. For Dedicated, pools are customer-isolated. For Private, it's under your network. Small caveat: where we route fallbacks to cheaper model variants, we ensure no customer data is used for other tenants — that is controlled by policy.
[05:07] Tariq: You mentioned fallbacks — if capacity constrained, could requests move to a different region? Data residency concern.
[05:13] Maya: Yes, by default we route within region. Fallback to other regions can be disabled per-tenant to ensure residency. We'll show routing policy config in the console.
[05:23] Leah: From a legal perspective, we need contract language on data deletion on termination. Can Redwood provide certification or a process?
[05:30] Carlos: We have a documented data deletion workflow with attestations. We'll share a template addendum that outlines deletion timelines and proof artifacts.
[05:39] Janelle: On logging, can we get per-token billing traces and per-request latency traces?
[05:44] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns and trace IDs you can correlate with your logs.
[05:52] Tariq: For the pilot, we'd like to run a 2-week benchmark on a subset of models and a representative dataset, with the ability to evaluate latency P50/P95 and per-token cost. Is that doable?
[06:03] Maya: Absolutely. Pilot scope: dedicate a small Dedicated pool or hosted sandbox with pinned model version, we'll instrument traces and share dashboard. Carlos will scope the bench.
[06:12] Carlos: We'll need dataset size, token distribution, and concurrency numbers. Also want to discuss quantization and batching options — these affect latency and cost.
[06:23] Tariq: We'll send a sample dataset and target concurrent sessions (approx 50 concurrent, bursts to 200).
[06:29] Janelle: A quick question — do you support customer-supplied model artifacts for private deployment? We may have IP we don't want to share.
[06:36] Carlos: For Private/on-prem, yes. You can deploy proprietary models in your environment; Redwood provides the runtime and orchestration but the model files remain in your control. For Hosted, we have model onboarding contracts and isolation guarantees but not typical for customer-supplied private models.
[06:52] Leah: Anything else from legal perspective — encryption in transit, breach notification SLA?
[06:58] Maya: We have a 72-hour breach notification policy for incidents affecting customer data, and our security incident response process is in the SOC2 docs. We can incorporate stricter SLAs in enterprise contracts.
[07:10] Janelle: Wrap-up — high level, looks promising. We'll need the certs and the SAML/SCIM docs and sample RBAC roles to evaluate.
[07:20] Maya: Will do. Carlos, any final notes?
[07:23] Carlos: I'll prepare the demo tenant and attach the exportable audit log examples. Also will include a short doc on KMS/BYOK options and what differs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[07:33] Tariq: Thanks — we'll push the dataset and requirements to Maya.
[07:36] Leah: We'll follow up on the legal checklist.
[07:39] Maya: Great. Next sync — tech deep-dive the week of Aug 11. I'll send calendar invite after this call. Thanks everyone.
[07:48] Janelle: Thanks all.
[07:50] (call ends)

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and speaker overlaps; references to KV cache sometimes transcribed as 'K-V cash' and SAML spelled 'Sam-el' in a couple places.
